sanskrit: sāraṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam balam ālokayan sarvaṃ śuko vākyam athābravīt
english: Having heard the words of Sāraṇa, Śuka then addressed Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, as he surveyed the entire army.

sanskrit: sthitān paśyasi yān etān mattān iva mahādvipān nyagrodhān iva gāṅgeyān sālān haimavatīn iva
english: Those whom you see standing there, like great elephants in rut, like banyan trees on the Gaṅgā's banks, like śāla trees of the Himālayas —

sanskrit: ete duṣprasahā rājan balinaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ daityadānavasaṃkāśā yuddhe devaparākramāḥ
english: — these, O king, are irresistible, mighty, and can change form at will; they are comparable to the Daityas and Dānavas, and in battle their valor equals that of the gods.

sanskrit: eṣāṃ koṭisahasrāṇi nava pañcaca sapta ca tathā śaṅkhasahasrāṇi tathā vṛndaśatāni ca
english: Of these there are nine thousand koṭis, five and seven koṭis besides, thousands upon thousands of śaṅkhas, and hundreds of vṛndas.

sanskrit: ete sugrīvasacivāḥ kiṣkindhānilayāḥ sadā harayo devagandharvair utpannāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
english: These are the ministers of Sugrīva, ever dwelling in Kiṣkindhā, vānaras born of gods and gandharvas, capable of assuming any form at will.

sanskrit: yau tau paśyasi tiṣṭhantau kumārau devarūpiṇau maindaś ca dvividaś cobhau tābhyāṃ nāsti samo yudhi
english: Those two princes whom you see standing there, of divine appearance — they are Mainda and Dvivida; in battle there is none equal to them.

sanskrit: brahmaṇā samanujñātāv amṛtaprāśināv ubhau āśaṃsete yudhā laṅkām etau marditum ojasā
english: Both were granted leave by Brahmā and have drunk the nectar of immortality; these two aspire to crush Laṅkā in battle by their own might.

sanskrit: yāv etāv etayoḥ pārśve sthitau parvatasaṃnibhau sumukho vimukhaś caiva mṛtyuputrau pituḥ samau
english: And those two who stand at their sides, resembling mountains — they are Sumukha and Vimukha, sons of Mṛtyu, equal to their father in power.

sanskrit: yaṃ tu paśyasi tiṣṭhantaṃ prabhinnam iva kuñjaram yo balāt kṣobhayet kruddhaḥ samudram api vānaraḥ
english: And that vānara whom you see standing there, like a great elephant in must — in his fury he could churn even the ocean by his strength.

sanskrit: eṣo 'bhigantā laṅkāyā vaidehyās tava ca prabho enaṃ paśya purā dṛṣṭaṃ vānaraṃ punar āgatam
english: This one came to Laṅkā before, O lord, on behalf of the Vaidehī and of you yourself — behold, this vānara has returned, the one you saw before.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhaḥ kesariṇaḥ putro vātātmaja iti śrutaḥ hanūmān iti vikhyāto laṅghito yena sāgaraḥ
english: He is the eldest son of Keśarin, known as the son of the Wind-god, celebrated by the name Hanūmān — the one by whom the ocean was leaped across.

sanskrit: kāmarūpī hariśreṣṭho balarūpasamanvitaḥ anivāryagatiś caiva yathā satatagaḥ prabhuḥ
english: A shape-shifter, foremost among the vānaras, endowed with strength and form, his movement is irresistible, like that of the ever-moving sun-god.

sanskrit: udyantaṃ bhāskaraṃ dṛṣṭvā bālaḥ kila pipāsitaḥ triyojanasahasraṃ tu adhvānam avatīrya hi
english: It is said that as a child, consumed by thirst, seeing the rising sun, he descended a path of three thousand yojanas —

sanskrit: ādityam āhariṣyāmi na me kṣut pratiyāsyati iti saṃcintya manasā puraiṣa baladarpitaḥ
english: — having resolved in his mind, 'I will seize the sun, and my hunger shall not return,' this one, drunk on his own power, leaped upward.

sanskrit: anādhṛṣyatamaṃ devam api devarṣidānavaiḥ anāsādyaiva patito bhāskarodayane girau
english: Unable to reach that god — unapproachable even by gods, seers, and dānavas — he fell upon the mountain at the sun's rising.

sanskrit: patitasya kaper asya hanur ekā śilātale kiṃ cid bhinnā dṛḍhahanor hanūmān eṣa tena vai
english: When this ape fell, one jaw was slightly fractured upon the rocky surface — he of the firm jaw — and it is for this that he is called Hanūmān.

sanskrit: satyam āgamayogena mamaiṣa vidito hariḥ nāsya śakyaṃ balaṃ rūpaṃ prabhāvo vānubhāṣitum
english: Truly, through the authority of scripture this vānara is known to me — his strength, his form, his power are impossible to describe in words.

sanskrit: eṣa āśaṃsate laṅkām eko marditum ojasā yaś caiṣo 'nantaraḥ śūraḥ śyāmaḥ padmanibhekṣaṇaḥ
english: This one aspires to crush Laṅkā single-handedly by his might. And the next hero, the dark one with lotus-like eyes —

sanskrit: ikṣvākūṇām atiratho loke vikhyāta pauruṣaḥ yasmin na calate dharmo yo dharmaṃ nātivartate
english: — a supreme chariot-warrior of the Ikṣvākus, whose valor is celebrated throughout the world, in whom dharma never wavers, and who never transgresses dharma —

sanskrit: yo brāhmam astraṃ vedāṃś ca veda vedavidāṃ varaḥ yo bhindyād gaganaṃ bāṇaiḥ parvatāṃś cāpi dārayet
english: — who knows the Brahmā-weapon and the Vedas, foremost among those versed in the Vedas, who could split the sky with his arrows and cleave the mountains asunder —

sanskrit: yasya mṛtyor iva krodhaḥ śakrasyeva parākramaḥ sa eṣa rāmas tvāṃ yoddhuṃ rājan samabhivartate
english: — whose wrath is like Death itself and whose valor rivals that of Śakra — that is Rāma, O king, who comes to fight you.

sanskrit: yaś caiṣa dakṣiṇe pārśve śuddhajāmbūnadaprabhaḥ viśālavakṣās tāmrākṣo nīlakuñcitamūrdhajaḥ
english: And he who stands at his right side, radiant as pure gold, broad-chested, copper-eyed, with dark and curling locks —

sanskrit: eṣo 'sya lakṣmaṇo nāma bhrātā prāṇasamaḥ priyaḥ naye yuddhe ca kuśalaḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ
english: — this is his brother Lakṣmaṇa, dear to him as his own life, skilled in statecraft and in battle, versed in every science of weapons.

sanskrit: amarṣī durjayo jetā vikrānto buddhimān balī rāmasya dakṣiṇo bāhur nityaṃ prāṇo bahiścaraḥ
english: He is intolerant of insult, unconquerable, a victor, valiant, wise, and strong — the right arm of Rāma, ever his outer breath of life.

sanskrit: na hy eṣa rāghavasyārthe jīvitaṃ parirakṣati eṣaivāśaṃsate yuddhe nihantuṃ sarvarākṣasān
english: For the sake of Rāghava he does not guard his own life; this one himself aspires to slay all the rākṣasas in battle.

sanskrit: yas tu savyam asau pakṣaṃ rāmasyāśritya tiṣṭhati rakṣogaṇaparikṣipto rājā hy eṣa vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: And he who stands supporting Rāma on his left flank, surrounded by a troop of rākṣasas — he is King Vibhīṣaṇa.

sanskrit: śrīmatā rājarājena laṅkāyām abhiṣecitaḥ tvām eva pratisaṃrabdho yuddhāyaiṣo 'bhivartate
english: Consecrated as king of Laṅkā by the glorious king of kings, it is against you alone that he comes forward, filled with righteous fury, ready for battle.

sanskrit: yaṃ tu paśyasi tiṣṭhantaṃ madhye girim ivācalam sarvaśākhāmṛgendrāṇāṃ bhartāram aparājitam
english: And he whom you see standing in the center, immovable as a mountain — the undefeated lord of all the kings of the monkey-troops —

sanskrit: tejasā yaśasā buddhyā jñānenābhijanena ca yaḥ kapīn ati babhrāja himavān iva parvatān
english: — who surpassed all the vānaras in splendor, fame, wisdom, knowledge, and nobility, as the Himālaya surpasses all other mountains —

sanskrit: kiṣkindhāṃ yaḥ samadhyāste guhāṃ sagahanadrumām durgāṃ parvatadurgasthāṃ pradhānaiḥ saha yūthapaiḥ
english: — who rules Kiṣkindhā, that cave overgrown with dense trees, an inaccessible stronghold set within a mountain fastness, together with his chief commanders —

sanskrit: yasyaiṣā kāñcanī mālā śobhate śatapuṣkarā kāntā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ desirous yasyāṃ lakṣmīḥ pratiṣṭhitā
english: — upon whom this golden garland of a hundred lotuses shines beautifully, lovely to gods and men alike, in whom Lakṣmī herself is established —

sanskrit: etāṃ ca mālāṃ tārāṃ ca kapirājyaṃ ca śāśvatam sugrīvo vālinaṃ hatvā rāmeṇa pratipāditaḥ
english: — this garland, and Tārā, and the eternal kingdom of the vānara king — all this Sugrīva received from Rāma after slaying Vālin.

sanskrit: evaṃ koṭisahasreṇa śaṅkūnāṃ ca śatena ca sugrīvo vānarendras tvāṃ yuddhārtham abhivartate
english: With such a force of a thousand koṭis and a hundred śaṅkus, Sugrīva, lord of the vānaras, advances against you for battle.

sanskrit: imāṃ mahārājasamīkṣya vāhinīm upasthitāṃ prajvalitagrahopamām tataḥ prayatnaḥ paramo vidhīyatāṃ yathā jayaḥ syān na paraiḥ parājayaḥ
english: Seeing this army now arrayed before you, O great king, blazing like a meteor in its splendor, let the utmost effort be made, so that there be victory and not defeat at the hands of the enemy.

sanskrit: śukena tu samākhyātāṃs tān dṛṣṭvā hariyūthapān samīpasthaṃ ca rāmasya bhrātaraṃ svaṃ vibhīṣaṇam
english: Having thus heard Śuka's account, and having seen those leaders of the vānara hosts, and his own brother Vibhīṣaṇa standing near Rāma —

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahāvīryaṃ bhujaṃ rāmasya dakṣiṇam sarvavānararājaṃ ca sugrīvaṃ bhīmavikramam
english: — and Lakṣmaṇa of tremendous might, the right arm of Rāma, and Sugrīva, king of all the vānaras, of terrible valor —

sanskrit: kiṃ cid āvignahṛdayo jātakrodhaś ca rāvaṇaḥ bhartsayām āsa tau vīrau kathānte śukasāraṇau
english: — Rāvaṇa, his heart somewhat disturbed and anger rising within him, at the conclusion of the report threatened those two heroes, Śuka and Sāraṇa.

sanskrit: adhomukhau tau praṇatāv abravīc chukasāraṇau roṣagadgadayā vācā saṃrabdhaḥ paruṣaṃ vacaḥ
english: As Śuka and Sāraṇa bowed with downcast faces, he spoke to them harsh words, his voice choked with rage, beside himself with fury.

sanskrit: na tāvat sadṛśaṃ nāma sacivair upajīvibhiḥ vipriyaṃ nṛpater vaktuṃ nigrahapragrahe vibhoḥ
english: It is not fitting for ministers who live by the king's favor to speak what is disagreeable to him who holds the power of punishment and reward, who is their lord.

sanskrit: ripūṇāṃ pratikūlānāṃ yuddhārtham abhivartatām ubhābhyāṃ sadṛśaṃ nāma vaktum aprastave stavam
english: For you two, it is utterly unsuitable to sing the praises of enemies who advance adversarially intent on battle, and to do so out of season.

sanskrit: ācāryā guravo vṛddhā vṛthā vāṃ paryupāsitāḥ sāraṃ yad rājaśāstrāṇām anujīvyaṃ na gṛhyate
english: Teachers, preceptors, and elders have been attended upon by you in vain, since you have failed to grasp the essence of the science of kingship — that which ministers must live by.

sanskrit: gṛhīto vā na vijñāto bhāro jñānasya vochyate īdṛśaiḥ sacivair yukto mūrkhair diṣṭyā dharāmy aham
english: Or perhaps it was grasped but not understood — such is called the burden of knowledge. By my fate I bear being yoked to foolish ministers such as these.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu mṛtyor bhayaṃ nāsti māṃ vaktuṃ paruṣaṃ vacaḥ yasya me śāsato jihvā prayacchati śubhāśubham
english: Is there no fear of death in you, that you would speak harsh words to me, whose very tongue, when I command it, delivers what is auspicious and inauspicious?

sanskrit: apy eva dahanaṃ spṛṣṭvā vane tiṣṭhanti pādapāḥ rājadoṣaparāmṛṣṭās tiṣṭhante nāparādhinaḥ
english: Trees may survive after touching fire and remain standing in the forest; but those who have been touched by a king's displeasure, if they have truly offended, do not survive.

sanskrit: hanyām aham imau pāpau śatrupakṣapraśaṃsakau yadi pūrvopakārair me na krodho mṛdutāṃ vrajet
english: I would slay these two sinners who sing the praises of the enemy's side, were my anger not softened by the remembrance of services they have rendered me before.

sanskrit: apadhvaṃsata gacchadhvaṃ saṃnikarṣād ito mama na hi vāṃ hantum icchāmi smarann upakṛtāni vām hatāv eva kṛtaghnau tau mayi snehaparāṅmukhau
english: Begone — depart from my presence! I do not wish to slay you, remembering the services you have done for me. Those two ungrateful ones who have turned their affections away from me would be as good as slain.

sanskrit: evam uktau tu savrīḍau tāv ubhau śukasāraṇau rāvaṇaṃ jayaśabdena pratinandyābhiniḥsṛtau
english: Addressed thus, both Śuka and Sāraṇa, filled with shame, congratulated Rāvaṇa with cries of victory and departed.

sanskrit: abravīt sa daśagrīvaḥ samīpasthaṃ mahodaram upasthāpaya śīghraṃ me cārān nītiviśāradān
english: Then the ten-necked one said to Mahodara who stood nearby: 'Quickly bring before me spies versed in statecraft.'

sanskrit: tataś carāḥ saṃtvaritāḥ prāptāḥ pārthivaśāsanāt upasthitāḥ prāñjalayo vardhayitvā jayāśiṣā
english: Then the spies, hastened by the king's command, arrived and stood before him with hands folded in salutation, wishing him victory and prosperity.

sanskrit: tān abravīt tato vākyaṃ rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ cārān pratyayikāñ śūrān bhaktān vigatasādhvasān
english: Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, then spoke to those spies — trustworthy, brave, devoted, and fearless.

sanskrit: ito gacchata rāmasya vyavasāyaṃ parīkṣatha mantreṣv abhyantarā ye 'sya prītyā tena samāgatāḥ
english: Go from here and ascertain Rāma's intentions; those who are privy to his counsels and have joined him with affection —

sanskrit: kathaṃ svapiti jāgarti kim anyac ca kariṣyati vijñāya nipuṇaṃ sarvam āgantavyam aśeṣataḥ
english: — how he sleeps, how he keeps watch, and what else he plans to do — learn all this with precision and return without omission.

sanskrit: cāreṇa viditaḥ śatruḥ paṇḍitair vasudhādhipaiḥ yuddhe svalpena yatnena samāsādya nirasyate
english: An enemy known through espionage is, by wise kings, confronted and repelled in battle with very little effort.

sanskrit: cārās tu te tathety uktvā prahṛṣṭā rākṣaseśvaram kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ jagmur yatra rāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ
english: The spies, saying 'So be it' and filled with enthusiasm, circumambulated the lord of the rākṣasas and went to where Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa were.

sanskrit: te suvelasya śailasya samīpe rāmalakṣmaṇau pracchannā dadṛśur gatvā sasugrīvavibhīṣaṇau
english: Going there, disguised, they beheld near Mount Suvela Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa together with Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa.

sanskrit: te tu dharmātmanā dṛṣṭā rākṣasendreṇa rākṣasāḥ vibhīṣaṇena tatrasthā nigṛhītā yadṛcchayā
english: Those rākṣasas, however, were spotted by Vibhīṣaṇa, that righteous lord of rākṣasas, and were apprehended where they stood, as if by chance.

sanskrit: vānarair arditās te tu vikrāntair laghuvikramaiḥ punar laṅkām anuprāptāḥ śvasanto naṣṭacetasaḥ
english: Manhandled by the vānaras — valiant, swift in their movements — they managed to return to Laṅkā, panting and out of their senses.

sanskrit: tato daśagrīvam upasthitās te cārā bahirnityacarā niśācarāḥ gireḥ suvelasya samīpavāsinaṃ nyavedayan bhīmabalaṃ mahābalāḥ
english: Then those spies, those night-wanderers who move perpetually abroad, presented themselves before the ten-necked one and reported to him of the terrible force of the mighty one encamped near Mount Suvela.

sanskrit: tatas tam akṣobhya balaṃ laṅkādhipataye carāḥ suvele rāghavaṃ śaile niviṣṭaṃ pratyavedayan
english: Then the spies reported to the lord of Laṅkā of that unassailable army, and of Rāghava encamped upon Mount Suvela.

sanskrit: cārāṇāṃ rāvaṇaḥ śrutvā prāptaṃ rāmaṃ mahābalam jātodvego 'bhavat kiṃ cic chārdūlaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Rāvaṇa, hearing from the spies of Rāma's arrival with his great army, became somewhat agitated and then spoke to Śārdūla.

sanskrit: ayathāvac ca te varṇo dīnaś cāsi niśācara nāsi kaccid amitrāṇāṃ kruddhānāṃ vaśam āgataḥ
english: Your complexion is unnatural and you appear dejected, O night-wanderer — have you perhaps fallen into the power of angered enemies?

sanskrit: iti tenānuśiṣṭas tu vācaṃ mandam udīrayat tadā rākṣasaśārdūlaṃ śārdūlo bhayavihvalaḥ
english: Thus instructed by him, Śārdūla, overwhelmed with fear, slowly began to speak to that tiger among rākṣasas.

sanskrit: na te cārayituṃ śakyā rājan vānarapuṃgavāḥ vikrāntā balavantaś ca rāghaveṇa ca rakṣitāḥ
english: Those foremost vānaras cannot be spied upon, O king — they are valiant, powerful, and are protected by Rāghava.

sanskrit: nāpi saṃbhāṣituṃ śakyāḥ saṃpraśno 'tra na labhyate sarvato rakṣyate panthā vānaraiḥ parvatopamaiḥ
english: Nor can one speak with them; no inquiry can be obtained there. Every path is guarded on all sides by those vānaras who are like mountains.

sanskrit: praviṣṭamātre jñāto 'haṃ bale tasminn acārite balād gṛhīto bahubhir bahudhāsmi vidāritaḥ
english: The moment I entered that army, which had not yet been spied upon, I was recognized, seized by force by many, and torn apart in many ways.

sanskrit: jānubhir muṣṭibhir dantais talaiś cābhihato bhṛśam pariṇīto 'smi haribhir balavadbhir amarṣaṇaiḥ
english: I was beaten heavily with knees, fists, teeth, and open palms, and dragged about by those powerful, wrathful vānaras.

sanskrit: pariṇīya ca sarvatra nīto 'haṃ rāmasaṃsadam rudhirādigdhasarvāṅgo vihvalaś calitendriyaḥ
english: Having been dragged everywhere, I was led before Rāma's assembly, my whole body smeared with blood, stupefied, my senses reeling.

sanskrit: haribhir vadhyamānaś ca yācamānaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ rāghaveṇa paritrāto jīvāmi ha yadṛcchayā
english: Even as the vānaras were killing me and I begged with folded hands, I was rescued by Rāghava — and so I live, it seems, by mere chance.

sanskrit: eṣa śailaiḥ śilābhiś ca pūrayitvā mahārṇavam dvāram āśritya laṅkāyā rāmas tiṣṭhati sāyudhaḥ
english: Having filled the great ocean with rocks and boulders, Rāma now stands armed at the very gate of Laṅkā.

sanskrit: garuḍavyūham āsthāya sarvato haribhir vṛtaḥ māṃ visṛjya mahātejā laṅkām evābhivartate
english: Having deployed in the garuḍa battle-formation, surrounded on all sides by vānaras, the great-souled one released me and now advances directly upon Laṅkā.

sanskrit: purā prākāram āyāti kṣipram ekataraṃ kuru sītāṃ cāsmai prayacchāśu suyuddhaṃ vā pradīyatām
english: Before he reaches the rampart, quickly do one of two things: either give Sītā back to him at once, or offer him worthy battle.

sanskrit: manasā saṃtatāpātha tac chrutvā rākṣasādhipaḥ śārdūlasya mahad vākyam athovāca sa rāvaṇaḥ
english: Inwardly burning with anguish upon hearing Śārdūla's momentous words, the lord of the rākṣasas, Rāvaṇa, then spoke.

sanskrit: yadi māṃ pratiyudhyeran devagandharvadānavāḥ naiva sītāṃ pradāsyāmi sarvalokabhayād api
english: Even if the gods, gandharvas, and dānavas were all to fight against me, I will not give back Sītā — not even out of fear of all the worlds.

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahātejā rāvaṇaḥ punar abravīt cāritā bhavatā senā ke 'tra śūrāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the great-souled Rāvaṇa spoke again: 'The army you have scouted — who among the leaping ones are the heroes there?'

sanskrit: kīdṛśāḥ kiṃprabhāvāś ca vānarā ye durāsadāḥ kasya putrāś ca pautrāś ca tattvam ākhyāhi rākṣasa
english: What are they like, and what is the power of those vānaras who are so difficult to assail? Whose sons and grandsons are they? Tell me the truth, O rākṣasa.

sanskrit: tatr atra pratipatsyāmi jñātvā teṣāṃ balābalam avaśyaṃ balasaṃkhyānaṃ kartavyaṃ yuddham icchatā
english: Having assessed their strength and weakness there, I shall formulate a response — for one who desires battle must necessarily take stock of the enemy's force.

sanskrit: athaivam uktaḥ śārdūlo rāvaṇenottamaś caraḥ idaṃ vacanam ārebhe vaktuṃ rāvaṇasaṃnidhau
english: Addressed thus by Rāvaṇa, Śārdūla, that foremost of spies, began to speak these words in Rāvaṇa's presence.

sanskrit: atharkṣarajasaḥ putro yudhi rājan sudurjayaḥ gadgadasyātha putro 'tra jāmbavān iti viśrutaḥ
english: There is the son of Ṛkṣarajas, O king, who is exceedingly hard to conquer in battle; and the son of Gadgada, known as Jāmbavān.

sanskrit: gadgadasyaiva putro 'nyo guruputraḥ śatakratoḥ kadanaṃ yasya putreṇa kṛtam ekena rakṣasām
english: Another son of Gadgada too is present, and a son of Bṛhaspati, the son of Śatakratu himself — by whose single son such slaughter of rākṣasas was wrought.

sanskrit: suṣeṇaś cāpi dharmātmā putro dharmasya vīryavān saumyaḥ somātmajaś cātra rājan dadhimukhaḥ kapiḥ
english: Suṣeṇa too, righteous of soul, a mighty son of Dharma, is there; and gentle Dadhimukha the vānara, son of the moon-god, O king.

sanskrit: sumukho durmukhaś cātra vegadarśī ca vānaraḥ mṛtyur vānararūpeṇa nūnaṃ sṛṣṭaḥ svayambhuvā
english: Sumukha, Durmukha, and the vānara Vegadarśin are also there — Death itself, no doubt, fashioned in the form of vānaras by the Self-born.

sanskrit: putro hutavahasyātha nīlaḥ senāpatiḥ svayam anilasya ca putro 'tra hanūmān iti viśrutaḥ
english: Nīla, son of the fire-god, is there himself as commander of the army; and the son of the wind-god, known as Hanūmān, is also present.

sanskrit: naptā śakrasya durdharṣo balavān aṅgado yuvā maindaś ca dvividaś cobhau balināv aśvisaṃbhavau
english: Aṅgada, the young and powerful grandson of Śakra, who is irresistible, is there; and both Mainda and Dvivida, powerful sons of the Aśvins.

sanskrit: putrā vaivasvatasyātra pañcakālāntakopamāḥ gajo gavākṣo gavayaḥ śarabho gandhamādanaḥ
english: Sons of Vivasvat are there — five of them, each resembling Death at the end of an age: Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Śarabha, and Gandhamādana.

sanskrit: śveto jyotirmukhaś cātra bhāskarasyātmasaṃbhavau varuṇasya ca putro 'tha hemakūṭaḥ plavaṃgamaḥ
english: Śveta and Jyotirmukha are there, both sprung from the sun-god himself; and Hemakūṭa the vānara, son of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: viśvakarmasuto vīro nalaḥ plavagasattamaḥ vikrānto vegavān atra vasuputraḥ sudurdharaḥ
english: Nala, the valiant son of Viśvakarman, foremost among the vānaras, is there; and the son of the Vasus, the valiant and swift Sudurdhara.

sanskrit: daśavānarakoṭyaś ca śūrāṇāṃ yuddhakāṅkṣiṇām śrīmatāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ śeṣān nākhyātum utsahe
english: Ten koṭis of heroic vānaras eager for battle, glorious sons of gods — the rest I dare not enumerate.

sanskrit: putro daśarathasyaiṣa siṃhasaṃhanano yuvā dūṣaṇo nihato yena kharaś ca triśirās tathā
english: This son of Daśaratha is a young man with a lion's frame — the one by whom Dūṣaṇa was slain, and Khara, and Triśiras as well.

sanskrit: nāsti rāmasya sadṛśo vikrame bhuvi kaś cana virādho nihato yena kabandhaś cāntakopamaḥ
english: There is no one in this world equal to Rāma in valor — the one by whom Virādha was slain, and Kabandha, who was like Death itself.

sanskrit: vaktuṃ na śakto rāmasya naraḥ kaś cid guṇān kṣitau janasthānagatā yena tāvanto rākṣasā hatāḥ
english: No man on earth is capable of recounting Rāma's virtues — the one by whom so many rākṣasas dwelling in Janasthāna were slain.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇaś cātra dharmātmā mātaṃgānām ivarṣabhaḥ yasya bāṇapathaṃ prāpya na jīved api vāsavaḥ
english: And Lakṣmaṇa here, righteous of soul, like a bull among elephants — once having come within the path of his arrows, even Vāsava himself would not survive.

sanskrit: rākṣasānāṃ variṣṭhaś ca tava bhrātā vibhīṣaṇaḥ parigṛhya purīṃ laṅkāṃ rāghavasya hite rataḥ
english: And foremost among rākṣasas, your own brother Vibhīṣaṇa, having accepted the city of Laṅkā, is devoted to the welfare of Rāghava.

sanskrit: iti sarvaṃ samākhyātaṃ tavedaṃ vānaraṃ balam suvele 'dhiṣṭhitaṃ śaile śeṣakārye bhavān gatiḥ
english: Thus the entire vānara army encamped on Mount Suvela has been described to you — for what remains to be done, you yourself are the authority.
